newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece says Turkish Cypriot shooting criminal.
newsitem.headline: Greece says Turkish Cypriot shooting criminal.

text.p: Greece sharply criticised Turkey on Sunday, saying Turkish Cypriot forces who shot dead a Greek Cypriot on the divided island of Cyprus acted like common criminals.
"We condemn the cold-blooded murder by the occupation forces which act like common criminals," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said in a statement.

Early on Sunday Turkish Cypriot soldiers shot and killed a Greek Cypriot man who had crossed 200 metres (yards) into the occupied northern part of Cyprus to collect snails, Greek and Cypriot authorities said.
The incident raised to four -- three Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot -- the number of people killed along the buffer zone since tension began to rise in August.

"This new criminal act proves that Turkey's choice is the creation of tension in the area. What else must happen for the international community to understand that as long as the Cyprus problem remains unsolved it will be a source of dangers in the area," Reppas said.

The killing occurred hours before the expected arrival of Sir David Hannay, Britain's special representative on the Cyprus problem, who is making another effort to breach the stalemate in the 22-year old Cyprus dispute.
The shooting happened at 0735 (0435 GMT) near the eastern end of the buffer zone, close to Achna village and territory controlled by British military bases.
Tension on the Mediterranean island has increased since two Greek Cypriots were killed by Turks during protests along the buffer zone in August.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 following a Greek-engineered coup on the island. A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.

The island's division is the main issue blocking better relations between NATO allies Greece and Turkey. They are also at odds over territorial and mineral rights in the Aegean Sea and have come close to war a number of times in recent years.
Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos told parliament on Saturday that Greece will spend billions of dollars on new arms in the next five years to deter Turkish ambitions on Greek territory.
He reiterated that any further Turkish moves against Cyprus would mean war with Greece.
